name: Market SMA Crossover
required_data: daily OHLCV, adjusted close, SMA20, SMA50
entry_logic: SMA20 crosses above SMA50 (flat->long) and no position is open.
exit_logic: SMA20 crosses back below SMA50 while long.
risk_logic: None in the source: no stop, no target. Position size is a fixed fraction of NAV.
adaptation_notes: No logic change. Upstream trades SPY/QQQ/IWM; here it runs on each NSE constituent in its own capital sleeve so the 18% sizing rule keeps its original meaning.
source_summary: Buy SMA(20) above SMA(50), sell on the reverse cross.

name: Market RSI Mean Reversion
entry_logic: RSI(14) below 35 with no open position.
exit_logic: RSI(14) above 60 while long.
risk_logic: None in the source (no stop or target). Exit is the RSI threshold, so the maximum adverse excursion is unbounded until the oscillator recovers.
adaptation_notes: No logic change. The upstream RSI(14) is produced server-side and is not published; this port uses Wilder RSI and exposes an SMA-RSI variant for sensitivity testing.
source_summary: Buy RSI(14) < 35, sell RSI(14) > 60 at market.

name: Limit RSI Dip Buyer
entry_logic: RSI(14) < 40 and flat: buy limit 1.5% below the signal bar close, GTD 3 bars.
exit_logic: While long: sell limit 3% above average entry, GTD 3 bars. No signal exit.
risk_logic: No stop. Fill risk is explicit: if the dip never trades, the order expires.
adaptation_notes: No logic change. Rounding uses ₹1 tick in the source (round(x, 2)); NSE equities also quote in ₹0.05 ticks, so round(x, 2) is retained unchanged.
source_summary: Passive limit dip buy at -1.5%, limit take-profit at +3%, 3-bar expiry.

name: Limit Trend Pullback
entry_logic: Close above SMA(50) and flat: buy limit 1% below close, GTD 2 bars.
exit_logic: Close below SMA(50) -> cancel and sell at MARKET. Otherwise take-profit limit at +4% above average entry, GTD 5 bars.
risk_logic: Trend break acts as the stop (no explicit stop price).
adaptation_notes: No logic change. The branch order matters and is preserved: trend failure is checked before the take-profit re-arm, exactly as upstream.
source_summary: Pullback limit entry in an uptrend, +4% limit target, market exit on SMA breach.

name: Stop Breakout Entry
entry_logic: Buy stop at 1.002 x the highest close of the prior 20 bars, GTD 5 bars.
exit_logic: Fixed time exit: market sell 10 bars after the position appears.
risk_logic: No stop-loss. The only risk control is the fixed holding period.
adaptation_notes: No logic change. 'Bars' are NSE trading sessions, so the 10-bar hold is 10 sessions rather than 10 calendar days as in the original ETF run.
source_summary: Buy-stop above the 20-bar high, hold 10 bars, exit at market.

name: Protective Stop Loss
entry_logic: SMA20 crosses above SMA50 and flat: market buy.
exit_logic: SMA20 crosses back below SMA50: cancel working orders and sell at market. A protective stop at -5% from average entry also exits.
risk_logic: Fixed 5% protective stop on average entry; the stop is re-armed if it is cancelled while a position remains open.
adaptation_notes: No logic change. Because the stop is a plain STOP (not stop-limit), a gap down fills at the worse open — identical to upstream.
source_summary: SMA(20/50) entry with a -5% protective stop and signal exit.

name: Stop-Limit Breakout
entry_logic: Buy stop-limit: trigger 1.002 x prior 20-bar high, limit 0.4% above the trigger, GTD 5 bars.
exit_logic: Fixed time exit: market sell 12 bars after entry.
risk_logic: The limit caps slippage but creates non-fill risk after a fast breakout.
adaptation_notes: No logic change. Trigger-then-limit behaviour on the activation bar is preserved: the fill reference is floored at the stop price, never at the pre-trigger open.
source_summary: Stop-limit breakout above the 20-bar high, 12-bar hold, market exit.

name: Stop-Limit Protection
entry_logic: SMA20 crosses above SMA50 and flat: market buy.
exit_logic: Protective stop-limit at -4% / limit -4.5% from average entry; signal exit at market.
risk_logic: The limit can leave the position unprotected after a gap - unbounded downside until either the limit trades or the trend signal flips.
adaptation_notes: No logic change. NSE circuit limits and illiquidity make the unfilled-limit scenario more likely than in the original US ETF universe; the exit report records any position still open at the end of the sample.
source_summary: SMA(20/50) entry with a -4%/-4.5% protective stop-limit.

name: Trailing Stop Trend
entry_logic: SMA20 crosses above SMA50 and flat: market buy at 15% of NAV.
exit_logic: 4% trailing stop placed once the position exists; reverse SMA cross cancels it and exits at market.
risk_logic: Trailing stop follows the highest high since placement, so realised loss is bounded by the 4% trail from the peak, not from entry.
adaptation_notes: No logic change. The trail anchors on intraday highs, so daily NSE candles are sufficient; intraday data is not required for this strategy.
source_summary: SMA(20/50) entry, 4% trailing-stop exit, reverse cross as hard exit.

name: Trailing Stop RSI
entry_logic: RSI(14) below 38 while flat and no pending order: market buy at 15% of NAV.
exit_logic: 5% trailing stop placed after entry; RSI(14) above 65 cancels it and exits at market.
risk_logic: Trail from the post-entry peak. The RSI>65 take-profit is checked only on bars where the trailing order is already live.
adaptation_notes: No logic change. RSI is computed locally: Wilder smoothing by default, with the alternative SMA-RSI variant selectable in config because the vendor indicator implementation is not published.
source_summary: RSI(14) < 38 entry with a 5% trailing stop and RSI > 65 exit.

name: Trailing Stop-Limit
entry_logic: SMA20 crosses above SMA50 and flat: market buy at 15% of NAV.
exit_logic: Trailing stop-limit: 4% of the close at placement as the trail distance, 0.5% of the close as the limit offset; reverse cross exits at market.
risk_logic: The limit leg refuses to sell below the activated limit, so a gap can leave the position open past the trail trigger.
adaptation_notes: No logic change. Trail distance and limit offset are recomputed in rupees from the bar close at placement, exactly as upstream; they are absolute amounts, not percentages, for the life of the order.
source_summary: SMA(20/50) entry with a trailing stop-limit exit sized off the entry-bar close.

name: Bracket Trend
entry_logic: SMA20 crosses above SMA50 and flat: BRACKET buy at 15% of NAV.
exit_logic: Take-profit limit at +6% of the entry-bar close and stop-loss at -3%, activated as a one-cancels-other pair after the entry fills; reverse cross cancels both and exits at market.
risk_logic: Fixed 2:1 reward/risk per trade. The bracket, not the trend signal, normally closes the trade.
adaptation_notes: No logic change. Bracket prices are derived from the signal bar close, so the take-profit and stop-loss are fixed before the next-bar entry fill. The distance from the actual fill price therefore differs slightly, exactly as upstream.
source_summary: SMA(20/50) entry with a +6%/-3% bracket exit.

name: Bracket RSI Reversion
entry_logic: RSI(14) below 35, flat, no pending order: BRACKET buy at 15% of NAV.
exit_logic: Take-profit limit at +4% and stop-loss at -2% of the signal-bar close, activated as an OCO pair; RSI(14) above 70 cancels both and exits at market.
risk_logic: Fixed 2:1 reward/risk. The RSI>70 exit overrides the bracket only when the position is still open.
adaptation_notes: No logic change. Wilder RSI is used by default (SMA-RSI selectable) because the vendor RSI implementation is not published; the documented impact is limited to threshold-crossing timing.
source_summary: RSI(14) < 35 entry with +4%/-2% bracket and RSI > 70 discretionary exit.

name: OCO Dip Or Breakout
entry_logic: Every 5th bar while flat and no live pair: submit a BUY LIMIT 2% below the close and a BUY STOP 2% above it under one OCO pair id, each GTD 5 bars.
exit_logic: Fixed 10-bar hold from the entry bar, then cancel everything and sell at market.
risk_logic: Direction-agnostic entry; the OCO guarantees only one leg can fill. No protective stop, so risk is the 10-bar holding window.
adaptation_notes: No logic change. Both legs are BUY legs sharing one OCO pair id, which is how upstream expresses the bracket; the fill engine cancels the sibling on the first fill. NSE daily price bands can leave the stop leg unfilled on limit-up sessions.
source_summary: OCO dip/breakout entry every 5 bars, 10-bar time exit.

name: Intraday 5m Bracket Reversion
entry_logic: 5-minute RSI(14) below 30 while flat and no bracket already live: BRACKET buy at 20% of NAV.
exit_logic: Take-profit limit at +0.6% and stop-loss at -0.4% of the signal-bar close, as an OCO pair. There is no time exit; a position can carry overnight if neither leg triggers.
risk_logic: 1.5:1 reward/risk per trade, very tight in absolute terms, so the NSE cost model dominates the edge.
adaptation_notes: Logic unchanged, but NSE intraday equity trades cannot carry overnight in a real account. The backtest deliberately does not add a session-close flat rule because that would change the strategy; the exit report flags every position carried past the session end so the mismatch is visible instead of hidden. Free 5m history is limited to roughly 30-60 days, so results are not comparable with daily strategies.
source_summary: 5-minute RSI(14) < 30 entry with a +0.6%/-0.4% bracket.

name: Intraday 30m Stop Breakout
entry_logic: BUY STOP at 1.001 x the highest high of the prior 12 bars, GTD 3 bars, 20% of NAV.
exit_logic: After 8 bars in the position, cancel all orders and sell at market.
risk_logic: No stop-loss; the only risk control is the fixed 8-bar horizon. Stacked stop orders can enlarge the position beyond the 20% target.
adaptation_notes: Logic unchanged, including the missing pending-order guard, which is documented rather than silently fixed. Two Indian-market caveats: intraday equity positions cannot legally be carried overnight, and NSE has no 30-minute bar native to the exchange - bars are resampled from 1-minute or 5-minute data, so the 12-bar high depends on the resampling convention. Positions open at the session end are flagged.
source_summary: 30-minute buy-stop breakout above the 12-bar high, 8-bar time exit.

name: Monthly Rotation
required_data: daily adjusted close, point-in-time universe membership
entry_logic: On the first bar of each new month, rank the universe by 126-bar momentum on adjusted close and buy the top 3 names at an equal share of NAV.
exit_logic: Same event: any held name that fell out of the top 3 is sold at market.
risk_logic: Concentration risk: only 3 names, re-ranked monthly, with no stop-loss at all.
adaptation_notes: Logic unchanged, three documented differences in execution context. (1) It runs in portfolio mode because the ranking is cross-sectional. (2) Iteration over the target set is sorted: upstream iterates a Python set, whose order is not guaranteed across runs, which would break reproducible backtests. (3) The NIFTY 50 membership snapshot is current, not point-in-time, so a name promoted to the index recently is ranked over its pre-membership history. That survivorship path is reported, not corrected.
source_summary: Monthly top-3 six-month momentum rotation over the whole universe, market orders.

name: Signal-Change Rotation
entry_logic: SMA20 crosses above SMA50 on this bar (previous state flat): market buy at 18% of NAV.
exit_logic: SMA20 crosses below SMA50: market sell the whole position.
risk_logic: No stop-loss. Exit latency equals the SMA(20/50) cross, which can be many bars after the peak.
adaptation_notes: No logic change, so the upstream quirk is preserved: unlike orders_01 it does not call cancel_all on the exit, which is harmless here because it never places a standing exit order. Crosses are detected from the persisted previous signal, so no bar is traded twice and no future bar is consulted.
source_summary: Long/flat SMA(20/50) crossover, market orders only, traded on flips.

name: FX Momentum (Standard Lots)
required_data: daily FX OHLC, per-instrument contract multiplier and lot size
entry_logic: Each bar: direction = sign(close - close 126 bars ago); target = direction x whole lots sized by ATR risk and a 20% notional cap.
exit_logic: No discrete exit; the position is reversed or resized whenever the target changes, via a signed market delta order.
risk_logic: 0.5% of NAV at risk per lot-distance move in ATR, with a hard 20% notional ceiling per pair.
adaptation_notes: Not adapted. NIFTY 50 constituents are cash equities with no lot unit, no perpetual direction flip, and no FX-style contract multiplier; upstream also states its accounting ignores FX margin, swap and bid/ask, so any rupee translation would measure a different thing. Retained here for completeness and to document why it is excluded from the NSE results.
source_summary: Six-month FX momentum, ATR/notional-capped whole lots, market orders.

name: Futures Donchian (Contracts)
required_data: daily futures OHLC, contract multiplier, reference initial margin
entry_logic: Long when close exceeds the prior 55-bar high, short when it breaks the prior 55-bar low, otherwise hold the current sign; target sized in whole contracts.
exit_logic: No stop; the position flips or resizes when price leaves the Donchian channel or the size limits change.
risk_logic: 0.5% NAV ATR risk, 25% notional cap and 15% margin cap, all applied simultaneously.
adaptation_notes: Not adapted. Roll handling, tick rounding, variation margin and continuous-contract construction are all absent from this engine and from upstream; substituting NIFTY 50 cash equities would silently drop the short leg (which needs an F&O account) and the contract multiplier. Retained here for completeness and to document the exclusion.
source_summary: 55-day Donchian breakout on continuous futures, contract-sized market orders.
